question.text: Vikram took an education loan in April 2022 for his daughter's MBA program and started repaying it from October 2022. He pays Rs.2,80,000 as interest on the education loan in FY 2024-25. Under Section 80E (old regime), what deduction can he claim?

answer.text: Rs.2,00,000 (capped at housing loan interest limit)
Rs.2,80,000 (full interest amount, no upper limit)
Rs.0 (deduction not available in the new regime)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 167 of the NISM Series X-B workbook, Section 80E provides deduction in respect of interest paid on a loan taken for higher education. It is available to individuals, the deduction equals the amount paid as interest with no upper limit, and it is not available under the new tax regime. Vikram's Rs.2,80,000 interest paid in FY 2024-25 under the old regime is therefore fully deductible. The Trap: Option A confuses 80E with 80C (which has a Rs.1.5L cap and covers loan principal, not interest). Option B confuses it with Section 24 housing-loan interest. Option D would apply only if the new tax regime had been chosen, since 80E is not available in the new regime. Note: Source-backed rule from page 167 of Series X-B: full interest amount, no upper limit, individual taxpayer, old regime only.
